Team — did a targeted review. Summary and suggested contractual language below.

Summary: 
- No immediate red-flags on sanctions: SkyBridge is a recognized US entity. The risk arises from their partner list; we need an assurance that no downstream reseller is on a denied-party or OFAC list. Recommend adding a warranty & a right-to-terminate provision.
- Data residency: Technical control is feasible. Recommend explicit SOW clause that logs for the SkyBridge integration are stored in the US region for the pilot and that Redwood will provide audit exports on request under NDA.

Suggested addendum language (short):
1) Partner Screening Warranty: "Customer represents and warrants that, to the best of its knowledge, any third-party resellers or sub-customers included in the scope are not subject to sanctions or export restrictions. Customer will promptly notify Redwood if it becomes aware of any such restriction."
2) Compliance Termination: "Redwood may suspend or terminate services for any identified sanctioned/denied party without liability; customer may terminate the SOW with pro rata refund if service is suspended due to customer-provided reseller non-compliance."
3) Data Residency Addendum: "For the duration of the pilot, logs and audit records related to Customer data will be stored in the US region (us-west-1). Redwood will provide exportable audit logs via secure transfer upon request subject to NDA."

If the team accepts the above, I can redline the SOW and the standard MSA. Commercially — with these mitigations, legal supports recommending exec approval for the 25% pilot concession.

Neha Kapoor
